svg.text: Concept 11 · top view, an example arrangement (a reconstruction: not a photo, not to scale) · pins and firmware unchanged (PIN-MAP 7)
A/B wires out of the box
the ECHO and LDR voltage dividers,
the pump MOSFET, the RS-485 RO divider
the 5 V USB cables go in
a short single wire from the screw
terminal labeled with the same GPIO
measure the distance between the two pin
rows with a ruler; a 38-pin board doesn't fit;
its DC jack and regulator aren't used
the ESP32 from its own charger,
the loads from the MB102, GND tied together
DHT22, PIR, LDR, HC-SR04, the soil
sensor outside or through the wall
tied at the wall hole; ferrules
with a multimeter; move group by
test each group through the dashboard
No 220 V mains power inside the box. The relay is only for this project's 5 V loads; a 220 V AC-DC module and mains cables don't go into the box.
This curriculum never asks you to touch 220 V: this project's relay, fan, pump, and servo use 5 V from the MB102.
Optional path: soldering. A soldered perfboard replaces the mini breadboard for small circuits; fewer push-in contacts to work loose.
Soldering safety (temperature, glasses, flux fumes, washing hands) is covered in the soldering part of Concept 11. The author didn't photograph or test this box.
